I looked at every screenshot cited below, plus the owner's 2026-10-24 live-match screenshot.

findings.title: Space key is swallowed during a match: pause-menu buttons and the instant-replays checkbox can't be used with Space, and the press is replayed as a pass or tackle on resume
findings.evidence:
src/client/input.ts:129-143. The window keydown handler calls e.preventDefault() for ' ' on line 136 and sets this.pass or this.tackle on lines 140-142. It never checks the event target or whether the game is paused. Native activation of the focused control is blocked, and the press is kept as game input.

pausespace2.cjs output:
- Resume without Space: ball still at feet (owner 9, speed 0).
- Space on the focused Resume button: pauseAfterSpace true (the menu stays open). After resuming with Enter: owner -1, ball speed 12.3 m/s, i.e. a pass fired by itself.
- In 3D, the checkbox reads 'true -> true' after Space, but a mouse click toggles it.

spacekeys.cjs output:
- Checkbox after Enter: true. After Space: true. Stored value: null. Keydown on the checkbox is defaultPrevented by the game.
- Space on the focused Menu button does not open the pause menu.
- Space on 'All controls': aria-expanded stays false. Enter works.

The 'Instant replays' checkbox is therefore not keyboard-operable at all (WCAG 2.1.1). Enter never toggles a checkbox and Space is blocked.

Screenshot /tmp/rt/a11y/out/kb-pause.png shows the pause card with Resume focused.
findings.repro:
NODE_PATH=/opt/node22/lib/node_modules node /tmp/rt/a11y/out/pausespace2.cjs
NODE_PATH=/opt/node22/lib/node_modules node /tmp/rt/a11y/out/spacekeys.cjs

By hand: start a match, press Esc, press Space on the focused Resume button. Nothing happens. Press Enter: play resumes and your player immediately passes or tackles.
findings.suggested_fix:
In src/client/input.ts keydown, return early without preventDefault or action when e.target is a BUTTON, INPUT, SELECT, TEXTAREA or A other than the canvas. This is the same pattern as shootout.ts:421/434 ('if (onButton) return; // let the focused button take it'). Also pass an isPaused() callback and ignore game keys while paused.

In src/client/matchView.ts setPaused (line 156), clear queued one-shot inputs (pass, tackle, shoot, loft, switch) when pausing.

Add an e2e test in tests/e2e/match.e2e.cjs: pause, Space on Resume closes the menu and the ball stays at feet; Space on #opt-replays toggles it.

findings.title: Screen readers never hear most cards: 56% of yellows and 78% of reds are overwritten by the free-kick announcement in the same tick
findings.evidence:
How it happens:
- src/client/a11y.ts:38-43 announce() empties the region, clears the previous 60 ms timer and starts a new one. A second call within 60 ms cancels the first message.
- src/sim/rules.ts judgeFoul pushes the card event(s) (issueCard) and then awardRestart's 'restart' event in the same tick.
- src/client/matchView.ts:389-392 calls announce(refereeCall(...)) once per event in a loop, so 'Free kick to X' or 'Penalty to X' replaces the card.

Headless sim, /tmp/rt/a11y/out/sim/cards2.ts over 120 CPU matches: 321 yellow calls, 180 never heard (56%). 27 red calls, 21 never heard. Example: seed 26 tick 11450, 'Second yellow, red card: K. Oberegger' replaced by 'Free kick to Åsstead Athletic'.

In the browser, announce.cjs injects a foul, card and restart in the same shape the sim produces. The announcer log shows only 'Free kick to Port Selhamn Town', while the HUD shows 'YELLOW CARD / L. HARTINGFELD' (/tmp/rt/a11y/out/announce-card.png). Sendings-off, which leave a side a man short, are almost never announced.
findings.suggested_fix:
Make announce() in src/client/a11y.ts merge rather than replace. If a message is still pending, set pending = pending + ' ' + text and keep the same timer.

Alternatively, in matchView.ts collect this frame's calls (cards first) plus the goal and half/full-time lines, and announce them once, joined, e.g. 'Yellow card: L. Hartingfeld. Free kick to Port Selhamn Town.'

Add a unit test that two announce() calls within 60 ms both reach the region text.

findings.title: Colour-blind players can't tell the teams apart in about 1 in 10 kit pairings (crimson/green, red/green, green/orange); avoidClash only checks RGB distance
findings.evidence:
src/meta/names.ts:269-273 has 12 KIT_COLORS. src/client/main.ts:264-274 avoidClash swaps kits only when the plain RGB Euclidean distance between primaries is under 120.

/tmp/rt/a11y/out/py/cvd.py (Machado 2009 matrices, CIEDE2000), all 132 ordered home/away pairs after avoidClash, pairs below ΔE00 12:
- normal vision: 0/132
- deuteranopia: 10/132
- protanopia: 6/132

Worst pairs:
- #9f1239 vs #166534: normal 62.6, deutan 2.8
- #0b7a3e vs #9f1239: deutan 4.5
- #c8102e vs #166534: protan 6.3
- #0b7a3e vs #ea580c: protan 8.1
- #166534 vs #7c2d12: deutan 8.4

That is 7 of 66 unordered pairings.

In a live 3D match (kits.cjs, club #166534/#ffffff vs ladder #9f1239/#93c5fd), /tmp/rt/a11y/out/cvd-greencrimson-deutan.png and -zoom.png show normal vision on top and deutan below. Both sides become dark-olive shirts with light shorts.

The only non-colour cue is the 1-2 px orange stamina bar over your own team. It is hidden outside play/kickoff/restart phases (aim3d.ts:308, 435) and in replays. Red vs green under protanopia: /tmp/rt/a11y/out/cvd-redgreen-protan.png. The radar is fine because it uses dots vs triangles.
findings.repro:
python3 -I /tmp/rt/a11y/out/py/cvd.py 12
NODE_PATH=/opt/node22/lib/node_modules node /tmp/rt/a11y/out/kits.cjs '#166534' '#ffffff' '#9f1239' '#93c5fd' greencrimson
python3 -I /tmp/rt/a11y/out/py/simimg.py /tmp/rt/a11y/out/kits-greencrimson-1280.png /tmp/rt/a11y/out/cvd-greencrimson-deutan.png deutan 119,180,1161,717
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace the RGB test in avoidClash (src/client/main.ts) with a perceptual one. Clash if min(ΔE under normal, protan and deutan simulation) < ~20, or the lightness difference is < ~15. Then try the away secondary and the neutral kits under the same test.

Also add a cheap non-colour team cue: a small home/away shape over every player, such as a dot vs a chevron like the radar, or a 'colour-blind kits' toggle. Optionally retune the clashing greens and crimsons in KIT_COLORS (src/meta/names.ts).

findings.title: Phone HUD targets are far below 44 px and tightly stacked: Menu is 76x23, the Cam chip 71x16 sits 4 px below it, and a near-miss tap on Menu flips the camera
findings.evidence:
phonetargets.cjs at 390x844 (touch, isMobile):
- #pause-btn: 76x23 at y22-45
- #cam-btn: 71x16 at y49-65
- zoom −/+ buttons: 32x32 at y69-101
- #juice-mute: 28x28

Rules responsible: hud.css:21-38, 97, 100, 105.

A tap 6 px under Menu's bottom edge printed 'paused? false camera broadcast -> end'. It switched to the end-to-end camera instead of pausing. Phones have no Esc key, so Menu is the only way to pause or forfeit. Crop: /tmp/rt/a11y/out/phone-hudtr-crop.png. The Pass/Shoot pads are 66x66, which is fine.
findings.suggested_fix:
In src/client/hud.css under @media (pointer: coarse):
- give .hud-menu, .pitch-cam, .pitch-zoom button and .pitch-wrap .juice-mute at least 44x44 hit areas (min-height/min-width, or a ::before with inset:-10px)
- keep at least 8 px between them, e.g. put Cam and zoom in a row left of Menu
- hide the 'Esc' kbd on touch

findings.title: The mouse cursor is hidden on the pitch, and its replacement, the orange ground ring, has 1.15:1 contrast against the grass (1.08:1 for protanopia)
findings.evidence:
styles.css:615 sets '#pitch { cursor: none }'. aim3d.ts:193 draws the pointer as RingGeometry(0.42, 0.56) in ORANGE #ff8a1c (aim3d.ts:36) with no dark edge. Name tags get an 8 px black stroke and the triangle a dark rim; the ring has neither.

pointer3.cjs, no ball, on /tmp/rt/a11y/out/pointer-noball.png:
- ring pixels mean rgb(235,142,32) vs grass rgb(74,173,60): 1.15:1 (WCAG 1.4.11 needs 3:1)
- protanopia: ring (171,151,0) vs grass (177,158,46): 1.08:1
- deuteranopia: 1.32-1.74:1

/tmp/rt/a11y/out/pointer-noball-protan.png shows the ring nearly vanishing. With the ball, the white reticle helps. Without it (tackling, switching, steering) the ring is the only cursor for the main control scheme.
findings.suggested_fix: In src/client/r3d/aim3d.ts, draw a dark outline ring (rgba(0,0,0,.7), about 0.06 m wider on each side) under the orange pointer ring, and/or a thin white inner ring, as the name tags already do. Alternatively, show a small OS cursor on the pitch (cursor: crosshair in styles.css:615) as a fallback.

The overflowing element is 'H3.mode-title right 324.1 "LEAGUE"' (styles.css:1098 and 1159, 20 px uppercase with letter-spacing). /tmp/rt/a11y/out/home-320-league.png shows LEAGUE running into the card edge. findings.title: Pass and Shoot buttons are focusable inside aria-hidden="true"
findings.evidence: src/client/matchView.ts:141-143 wraps #pad-pass and #pad-shoot (focusable buttons) in '<div class="touch-pad" aria-hidden="true">'. Phone Tab order (matchtab.cjs phone) stops on both, at stops 5 and 6. This breaks the axe rule aria-hidden-focus.
findings.suggested_fix: Add tabindex="-1" to both pad buttons, since they are pointer-only, or remove aria-hidden and give Shoot an aria-label like Pass's.

findings.title: In-match labels and hints name the wrong input
findings.evidence:
- The HUD menu button's accessible name is 'Esc MENU' (AX tree), and it shows an Esc keycap on phones (hud.ts:57).
- The instant-replay hint says 'click to skip' even for keyboard players, who can also skip with Space, Enter or Esc (matchView.ts:256; seen in /tmp/rt/a11y/out/replay-reduce.png).
- The screen-reader line 'Replay. Goal · T. Thornton 1'.' never says how to skip (matchView.ts:260).
- On touch devices the canvas aria-label still describes only mouse and keys (matchView.ts:128).
findings.repro:
NODE_PATH=/opt/node22/lib/node_modules node /tmp/rt/a11y/out/matchtab.cjs desk (AX names)
NODE_PATH=/opt/node22/lib/node_modules node /tmp/rt/a11y/out/goalrm.cjs reduce (announcements)
findings.suggested_fix:
- In hud.ts, set aria-label="Menu" with the kbd aria-hidden, and hide the kbd under pointer:coarse.
- In matchView.ts, use 'click or press Space to skip' for non-coarse pointers and announce 'Replay … Press Escape to skip.'
- Use TOUCH_HINT wording for the canvas aria-label on coarse pointers.

findings.title: With prefers-reduced-motion, instant replays still start automatically with a pitch-level tracking camera and hard cuts
findings.evidence:
goalrm.cjs with reducedMotion 'reduce' logs camera modes ["broadcast","replay-low","replay-goal","broadcast"]. The replay plays in full.

camera3d.ts replayShot puts the eye 7 m up and 24 m off the ball, tracking it, then cuts behind the goal. instantReplaysPref() (matchView.ts:50) ignores prefers-reduced-motion.

Shake and confetti are correctly suppressed: no .pitch-wrap animation under reduce; with no preference it is waapi 520 ms.
findings.suggested_fix: In src/client/matchView.ts instantReplaysPref(), return false when there is no stored preference and prefers-reduced-motion matches. The pause-menu toggle still turns replays on. Alternatively, under reduce, play replays from the broadcast camera with no cuts (src/client/r3d/camera3d.ts).

good: Keyboard-only flow works: Tab reaches Kick off in 4 presses (skip link, level badge, Home tab, Kick off), WASD and Space play the match, and after full time focus lands on the result title with no ring.
Result dialog: Tab stays inside it, Esc closes it, and focus goes back to the control that started the match. Level-up and season-review dialogs use the same code.
Pause dialog: focus moves to Resume, Tab is trapped, Esc toggles it, and focus returns to the pitch canvas.
Replay viewer: a proper modal with a labelled scrubber, aria-keyshortcuts, a focus trap, and Esc returning focus to the 'Watch goals' button.
All 7 management screens, the pause menu and the result dialog have no unnamed controls and text contrast of at least 5.03:1 in light and dark. Focus rings are visible on every stop.

Goals, half-time, full-time, offsides and replays are announced through a persistent polite live region outside #app. Result stat rows carry screen-reader sentences, and the dialog is described by a score line.
Reduced motion: no screen shake or confetti, CSS animations are neutralised globally, and the camera moves more slowly.
The radar tells teams apart by shape (dots vs triangles), and name tags and stamina bars have dark outlines.
No horizontal scroll at 390 px or at 200% zoom on any screen, and forced-colors mode stays usable.
